title: Data Centers Are the Growth Engine of America’s Power Grid
title_zh: 資料中心成了美國電網的成長引擎
subtitle: 資料中心成了美國電網的成長引擎
author: Dow Jones Newswires

sentences.en: Backlash against data-center construction is raising questions about the future of America’s AI build-out.
sentences.zh: 反對興建資料中心的聲浪，讓人開始質疑美國 AI 擴建的未來。

sentences.en: For the power grid, the picture isn’t as murky—data centers are by far the biggest growth engine.
sentences.zh: 對電網來說，情況並沒有那麼模糊：資料中心顯然是最大的成長引擎。

sentences.en: They are vacuuming up electricity at a historic clip, ending decades of static power usage and reshaping who is plugging into the grid.
sentences.zh: 它們正以史上少見的速度吞吃電力，終結數十年來幾乎停滯的用電量，並改寫誰在接入電網。

sentences.en: Nationally, electricity use by commercial customers—a broad category that includes data centers—is poised to surpass residential demand this year for the first time, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
sentences.zh: 根據美國能源資訊署，全國商業用戶（這是一個包含資料中心的廣義類別）的用電量，今年可望首度超過住宅需求。

sentences.en: Residential and industrial—including things like factories, refineries and agriculture—are the other big categories.
sentences.zh: 住宅與工業（包括工廠、煉油廠和農業等）則是另外兩大類。

sentences.en: As investors start to trade the AI company’s shares, they may encounter some very different market-capitalization figures, depending on what source they are using.
sentences.zh: 當投資人開始交易這家 AI 公司的股票時，可能會碰到差異很大的市值數字，這取決於他們用的是哪一個來源。

sentences.en: The United Arab Emirates’ economy is expected to grow 7.3% in 2027 after expanding just 0.2% this year, assuming regional disruptions ease, the International Monetary Fund says.
sentences.zh: 國際貨幣基金組織表示，若地區動盪趨緩，阿拉伯聯合大公國經濟在今年僅成長 0.2% 之後，2027 年可望成長 7.3%。

sentences.en: Hydrocarbon growth is projected at 13.3% next year, compared with 2.3% in 2026, while nonoil activity is expected to grow 5.4% after contracting 0.5% this year.
sentences.zh: 碳氫產業成長預估明年為 13.3%，高於 2026 年的 2.3%；非石油活動在今年萎縮 0.5% 之後，預期將成長 5.4%。

sentences.en: Despite recent analysis suggesting that France’s economic woes are overblown, its public finances remain under significant pressure, Andrew Kenningham at Oxford Economics says in a note.
sentences.zh: 牛津經濟研究院的安德魯・肯尼厄姆在一份報告中表示，儘管近期分析認為法國的經濟困境被誇大了，其公共財政仍承受巨大壓力。

sentences.en: “If our forecasts are accurate, France would need to run a broadly balanced primary budget by 2030 if its debt is to be on a stable trajectory at that point,” Kenningham says.
sentences.zh: 肯尼厄姆說：「如果我們的預測正確，法國若要在 2030 年讓債務走在穩定軌道上，就必須在那時讓初級預算大致平衡。」

vocab.usage: backlash against 對…的強烈反彈；public backlash 輿論反彈
vocab.example: The tax hike triggered a backlash from small businesses.
vocab.example_zh: 這次加稅引發了小企業的強烈反彈。

vocab.usage: the AI build-out AI 基礎設施的擴建；network build-out 網路鋪設
vocab.example: The fiber build-out will take three more years.
vocab.example_zh: 光纖網路的擴建還要再花三年。

vocab.usage: the picture isn’t as murky 情況沒有那麼不明朗；murky water 混濁的水
vocab.example: The rules around the new tax credit are still murky.
vocab.example_zh: 這項新稅額抵減的規定仍然模糊不清。

vocab.zh: 成長引擎；帶動成長的主力
vocab.usage: the biggest growth engine 最大的成長引擎；a growth engine for the economy 經濟的成長引擎
vocab.example: Exports have become the country’s main growth engine.
vocab.example_zh: 出口已成為這個國家主要的成長引擎。

vocab.usage: at a historic clip 以史上少見的速度；at a rapid clip 快速地；另一義是「影片片段」
vocab.example: Orders are coming in at a rapid clip this quarter.
vocab.example_zh: 這一季訂單正快速湧入。

vocab.usage: static power usage 幾乎沒有變化的用電量；static prices 停滯的價格；名詞 static 也可指「靜電、雜訊」
vocab.example: Sales were static for most of the year.
vocab.example_zh: 這一年大部分時間，銷售都停滯不前。

vocab.usage: reshape who is plugging into the grid 改寫誰在接入電網；reshape the industry 重塑產業
vocab.example: Remote work is reshaping demand for office space.
vocab.example_zh: 遠距工作正在改寫辦公室的需求。

vocab.usage: poised to surpass 可望超過；poised to launch 即將推出
vocab.example: The startup is poised to launch its first product next month.
vocab.example_zh: 這家新創下個月即將推出第一款產品。

vocab.usage: surpass residential demand 超過住宅需求；surpass expectations 超出預期
vocab.example: This year’s sales have already surpassed the full-year target.
vocab.example_zh: 今年的銷售已經超過全年目標。

vocab.usage: oil refineries 煉油廠；a sugar refinery 製糖廠
vocab.example: The oil refinery was shut down for repairs.
vocab.example_zh: 那座煉油廠因維修而關閉。

vocab.usage: market-capitalization figures 市值數字；常簡稱 market cap
vocab.example: The company’s market capitalization fell below $50 billion.
vocab.example_zh: 這家公司的市值跌破 500 億美元。

vocab.usage: regional disruptions 地區動盪；supply-chain disruptions 供應鏈中斷
vocab.example: Shipping disruptions pushed prices higher.
vocab.example_zh: 運輸中斷推升了價格。

vocab.zh: 碳氫化合物；石油天然氣產業
vocab.usage: hydrocarbon production / growth 油氣生產／成長；hydrocarbon sector 油氣產業
vocab.example: The country’s budget still depends on hydrocarbon exports.
vocab.example_zh: 這個國家的預算仍依賴油氣出口。

vocab.usage: activity contracted 0.5% 活動萎縮 0.5%；the economy contracted 經濟收縮；名詞 contract 是「合約」
vocab.example: Manufacturing output contracted for a third month.
vocab.example_zh: 製造業產出連續第三個月萎縮。

vocab.usage: woes are overblown 困境被誇大了；overblown fears 被誇大的恐懼
vocab.example: He argued that fears of a recession were overblown.
vocab.example_zh: 他認為對衰退的擔憂被誇大了。

vocab.usage: a stable trajectory 穩定的軌道；growth trajectory 成長軌跡
vocab.example: The debt is not on a stable trajectory.
vocab.example_zh: 債務並未走在穩定的軌道上。

vocab.usage: a deficit of 3% of GDP 相當於國內生產毛額 3% 的赤字；trade deficit 貿易逆差
vocab.example: The government promised to cut the budget deficit.
vocab.example_zh: 政府承諾要削減預算赤字。

vocab.usage: market volatility 市場波動；high volatility 高波動
vocab.example: High volatility makes it harder to plan investments.
vocab.example_zh: 高波動讓投資規劃變得更難。

vocab.usage: defensive names / stocks 防禦型股票；a defensive strategy 防守策略
vocab.example: Investors moved into defensive stocks during the selloff.
vocab.example_zh: 在這波下跌中，投資人轉進防禦型股票。

vocab.usage: amass a $100 billion portfolio 累積 1,000 億美元的投資組合；amass a fortune 累積財富
vocab.example: She amassed a large collection of first-edition books.
vocab.example_zh: 她累積了一批數量可觀的初版書。
